prediction.likelyOutcome: Quantum is favored to recover the bulk of its unpaid $24,179.35 final invoice from Plaza de Kaza (and possibly Dykstra depending on the agency finding), because the traffic-circle defect it withheld payment over appears to have been identified, agreed to be remediated, and actually repaired by agreement in November 2018 before suit was filed. Plaza de Kaza's counterclaim faces real liability headwinds (shared fault with the excavator/basin placement, an apparent cure) and, more fundamentally, has no quantified damages in this record, so any setoff is likely to be modest rather than a wash-out of the invoice.

figures.label: Unpaid balance of final invoice
figures.quote: Darehshori, however, stated that he refused to pay the remaining $24,179.35 balance because Quantum did not correctly pour the traffic circle

issues.label: Plaza de Kaza's Counterclaim: Defective Traffic Circle Curbing

outcome.description: After a three-day bench trial the court found Dykstra breached his agreement with Quantum and Plaza de Kaza was unjustly enriched, and entered judgment against both for $24,179.35 (the full final invoice, no setoffs), rejecting Plaza de Kaza's counterclaims; Quantum's later motion for attorney-fee sanctions was denied. The Court of Appeals affirmed (Quantum's challenges to the lien dismissal and the sanctions ruling failed).

source.caseName: Quantum Concrete, Inc. v. Plaza de Kaza, LLC, and Ronald A. Dykstra, d/b/a Dykstra Homes
